task: Week 6, Task 23 - Phase C: Detection & Analysis
detection_source_note: GuardDuty unavailable on account (Free tier, SubscriptionRequiredException). All findings derived from AWS CloudTrail via 'aws cloudtrail lookup-events', substituting for the GuardDuty-based workflow in the original task brief.

findings.title: IAM Self- and Role-Enumeration by Low-Privilege User
findings.description: User kerrigan attempted to enumerate her own attached and inline policies (denied), then successfully listed IAM roles and instance profiles in the account, revealing cg-ec2-meek-role and cg-ec2-mighty-role and their associated instance profiles.

findings.title: Privilege Escalation via IAM Instance Profile Role Swap
mitre_attack: T1098.003 - Account Manipulation: Additional Cloud Roles
findings.description: After a denied attempt to create a new instance profile, kerrigan removed the low-privilege cg-ec2-meek-role from the existing cg-ec2-meek-instance-profile and attached the higher-privilege cg-ec2-mighty-role to the same profile. This is a direct privilege escalation path: a user with iam:AddRoleToInstanceProfile / iam:RemoveRoleFromInstanceProfile but without iam:PassRole restrictions can redirect an existing instance profile to a more privileged role.

findings.title: Compute Resource Creation to Obtain Elevated Credentials
mitre_attack: T1578.002 - Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure: Create Cloud Instance
findings.description: kerrigan launched an EC2 instance with the now-escalated instance profile attached, allowing any process on that instance to retrieve cg-ec2-mighty-role credentials via the EC2 instance metadata service (IMDS). Interactive logon (SSH) followed by an IMDSv2 credential request confirmed the escalation: 'aws sts get-caller-identity' returned an assumed-role identity for cg-ec2-mighty-role-cgidjij1nc9chc.

findings.title: Persistence of Escalated Access Across Instance Replacement
mitre_attack: T1578.002 - Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure: Create Cloud Instance
findings.description: The original exploitation instance (i-058ab9689ac3248ad) was terminated and a second instance (i-0e7fe695da62fad3a) was launched with the same escalated instance profile and an attacker-imported SSH key pair, demonstrating that the escalation path persists at the instance-profile/role level and can be re-exploited independently of any single compute instance.

evidence_events.detail: i-0e7fe695da62fad3a launched with cg-ec2-meek-instance-profile and imported key pair cloudgoat-key
EC2 service re-assumed cg-ec2-mighty-role-cgidjij1nc9chc for the new instance

detection_gap_note: A read-only attempt to view the mighty role's own policies (ListAttachedRolePolicies, ListRolePolicies at 10:02-10:03) was denied, meaning kerrigan could not directly inspect what she was escalating into - she had to prove the escalation empirically via GetCallerIdentity from the assumed role itself. This illustrates that IAM write/attach permissions on a resource do not require read permissions on that same resource, which complicates manual review and increases reliance on CloudTrail for detection.
